    Constructing the double-cohook common corner #

    Starting with a negative left-boundary extension and then a negative right-boundary extension, this file restricts and replays the two suffixes to construct the other one-ended word. Both routes recover the same common corner, giving the literal double-cohook Butler--Ringel square.

    source

    SignedPath D.source corner.target

    Delete the negative left extension while retaining the negative right suffix of the common corner.
